_doc: Knowledge base for the crop image scanner. Keys match the classes the vision model is trained on. Chemical names are common active ingredients; always follow the product label and local agriculture-extension (KVK) advice.

healthy.name: Healthy leaf
healthy.symptoms: uniform green colour, no spots, no holes, no powdery coating, normal leaf shape
healthy.cause: No disease, pest or major nutrient stress detected in the visible area.
treatment: No treatment needed.
prevention: Keep scouting the field every 5-7 days, especially after rain.
Maintain balanced fertilisation and avoid water stress.
Remove weeds that harbour pests and diseases.
healthy.advice: Continue the current irrigation and nutrient plan.

leaf_blight.name: Leaf blight (necrotic blight)
leaf_blight.symptoms: large irregular brown or tan dead patches that spread from tips and margins, tissue drying and collapsing
leaf_blight.cause: Fungal or bacterial blight (e.g. Helminthosporium, Alternaria, Xanthomonas) favoured by warm, humid, wet-leaf conditions.
treatment: Remove and destroy badly affected leaves.
Spray mancozeb 75% WP at 2.5 g/L water, or copper oxychloride 50% WP at 3 g/L; repeat after 10-12 days if wet weather continues.
For bacterial blight use copper-based spray with streptocycline as per label.
prevention: Use certified disease-free seed and resistant varieties.
Avoid overhead irrigation late in the day.
Keep plant spacing wide enough for airflow.
Rotate with non-host crops.
leaf_blight.advice: Reduce nitrogen top-dressing until the outbreak is controlled and improve field drainage.

leaf_spot.name: Leaf spot
leaf_spot.symptoms: many small dark brown or black round spots, often with a yellow halo, scattered over the leaf
leaf_spot.cause: Fungal leaf spots (Cercospora, Septoria, Alternaria, early blight) spread by rain splash and humid weather.
treatment: Pick off heavily spotted leaves.
Spray chlorothalonil 75% WP at 2 g/L or mancozeb 75% WP at 2.5 g/L at 10-14 day intervals.
Neem oil 3 ml/L is an option for light infection.
prevention: Drip or furrow irrigation instead of sprinklers.
Mulch to stop soil splash.
Clear crop residue after harvest.
Rotate crops every season.
leaf_spot.advice: Spots on lower leaves first usually means splash from soil; mulching and staking helps.

powdery_mildew.name: Powdery mildew
powdery_mildew.symptoms: white or grey powdery coating on the leaf surface, patches that merge, leaves curling and yellowing
powdery_mildew.cause: Powdery-mildew fungi (Erysiphe, Podosphaera, Leveillula); thrives in dry leaf surfaces with high air humidity and moderate temperatures.
treatment: Spray wettable sulphur 80% WP at 2-3 g/L (not above 30 C).
Alternatively hexaconazole 5% EC at 2 ml/L or azoxystrobin as per label.
Potassium bicarbonate or diluted milk spray (1:9) can slow light infection.
prevention: Plant resistant varieties.
Avoid excess nitrogen that produces soft growth.
Improve spacing and airflow.
Scout early; mildew spreads quickly.
powdery_mildew.advice: Treat at the first white patches; late treatment gives poor control.

rust.name: Rust
rust.symptoms: small orange, rusty-brown powdery pustules on leaf surfaces, sometimes in rows, leaves yellowing around pustules
rust.cause: Rust fungi (Puccinia, Uromyces); wind-borne spores, cool nights with dew and moderate temperatures.
treatment: Spray propiconazole 25% EC at 1 ml/L or tebuconazole 25.9% EC at 1 ml/L.
Mancozeb 75% WP at 2.5 g/L can be used as a protective spray.
Repeat after 12-15 days if new pustules appear.
prevention: Grow rust-resistant varieties and sow on time.
Destroy volunteer plants and alternate hosts.
Balanced N-P-K; avoid late heavy nitrogen.
rust.advice: Rust spreads by wind, so alert neighbouring fields and treat the whole block.

nitrogen_deficiency.name: Nitrogen deficiency
nitrogen_deficiency.symptoms: uniform pale green to yellow leaves, older leaves yellowing first, stunted slow growth, no distinct spots
nitrogen_deficiency.cause: Insufficient plant-available nitrogen: leaching on sandy soils, waterlogging, low organic matter or too little fertiliser.
treatment: Top-dress urea at 40-50 kg N/ha (about 90-110 kg urea/ha) and irrigate lightly.
Quick fix: foliar spray of 2% urea (20 g/L) once or twice, 7 days apart.
Add compost or vermicompost to build slow-release nitrogen.
prevention: Split nitrogen into 2-3 doses.
Include legumes in rotation.
Avoid waterlogging that causes N loss.
nitrogen_deficiency.advice: Test soil nitrogen and follow the Fertilizer page for crop-specific doses.

potassium_deficiency.name: Potassium deficiency
potassium_deficiency.symptoms: yellow then brown scorched leaf edges and margins, older leaves first, spots near edges, weak stems
potassium_deficiency.cause: Low available potassium, common in sandy, leached or heavily cropped soils; worsened by drought stress.
treatment: Apply muriate of potash (MOP) at 40-60 kg K2O/ha as side-dressing.
Foliar spray of 1% potassium sulphate or 1% MOP for quick relief.
Add well-rotted farmyard manure.
prevention: Soil-test every 2-3 seasons.
Return crop residues to the field.
Maintain adequate soil moisture.
potassium_deficiency.advice: Potassium also improves disease and drought tolerance, so correct it before the next crop.

pest_damage.name: Pest damage (chewing insects)
pest_damage.symptoms: holes, ragged chewed edges and missing leaf tissue, irregular gaps in the leaf blade
pest_damage.cause: Chewing insects such as caterpillars, leaf beetles, grasshoppers or snails feeding on the foliage.
treatment: Inspect the underside of leaves and soil at dusk for larvae and beetles; hand-pick where practical.
Neem seed kernel extract 5% or neem oil 5 ml/L as first line.
Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) for caterpillars; spinosad or emamectin benzoate 5% SG at 0.4 g/L if above economic threshold.
prevention: Install pheromone or light traps for monitoring.
Encourage natural enemies (birds, ladybirds, spiders).
Clean weeds and crop residues.
Rotate crops.
pest_damage.advice: Spray only when damage crosses the economic threshold to protect beneficial insects.

mosaic_virus.name: Mosaic virus
mosaic_virus.symptoms: mottled light and dark green or yellow mosaic pattern, puckered or distorted leaves, stunted plants
mosaic_virus.cause: Plant viruses spread by aphids, whiteflies and infected seed or tools; there is no chemical cure.
treatment: Uproot and destroy infected plants (do not compost).
Control insect vectors: neem oil 5 ml/L or imidacloprid 17.8% SL at 0.3 ml/L for whitefly and aphids.
Disinfect tools; wash hands after handling infected plants.
prevention: Use virus-free certified seed and resistant varieties.
Use yellow sticky traps and reflective mulch.
Control weeds that host virus and vectors.
mosaic_virus.advice: Remove sick plants early; spraying cannot cure them and only protects healthy neighbours from vectors.
